title: An Appeal to the Gods at the Tower
type: A gathering at the Tower of Gael and petitions for a divine audience
dek: Scribonia gathers companions to ask the gods for answers. The appeal exposes different reasons for fighting, strained friendships and the care waiting between arguments.

facts.Recorded span: 27–28, Month of Death · Year 3 of the Final War
facts.Gathering: Scribonia, Adelia, Elenia, Arjahn, Nymera, Olokun, Oya and Alyhotep
facts.What is established: The company gathers, argues, makes petitions and disperses
facts.What remains open: The requested audience, any identified divine response and the later narrator prompts

events: The Tower’s company petitions for a divine audience

body:
A request first discussed by the exhausted company in Babel brings old companions together at the Tower of Gael. Some want explanations, some want reassurance and some want to know why they were chosen. Before any answer comes, they have to get through a difficult conversation with one another.

Portals, embraces and an impatient request

Scribonia steps into the Tower of Gael through a portal with two companions, then calls for Adelia. He wants clerics to help petition the gods for a meeting. He has heard an account from Dumuzi and wants to compare it with what the gods themselves will say.

The room does not become solemn immediately. Oya runs toward Olokun with open arms, pushes past him and embraces Nymera instead. Olokun objects to his own sister rejecting his hug; Oya eventually gives him one and says she was joking. Nymera quietly checks whether Oya seems hurt, says she missed her and asks about the letter.

Scribonia calls Elenia away from her materials and brings Arjahn into the gathering. Adelia thanks him for being honest with her and offering guidance. He surprises her by initiating a hug, stays in the group embrace for a while, then steps back when it becomes too much.

Adelia says she has safeguards against interplanar travel and asks to be warned next time. When Arjahn assumes the Tower is her domain, she corrects him: she says she is strongest near Hope and weaker where they are sitting. She proposes moving closer to the tree. The surviving sequence does not show that move before the petitions begin.

Different reasons to ask, and a friendship under strain

Scribonia wants an account of history, the selection of arrivals through the Gate and the state of the war. He says he does not believe Dumuzi and wants to give the gods an opportunity to answer. A representative would do; he is not asking them to abandon their work for an immediate appearance.

Elenia thinks some questions have already been answered and dislikes asking busy gods to repeat themselves. She is sarcastic about Scribonia giving them the benefit of the doubt. He is hurt by the contempt he hears in her response and asks what he has done to deserve it.

She explains that the gods are individuals and that asking them collectively to account for one another’s actions is unfair. Scribonia answers that the company’s leaders also bear responsibility for one another. She later accuses him of trying to make himself a judge of the divine; he rejects that description. The argument ends without either accepting the other’s account of his motives.

Arjahn has his own reason for wanting their words. He says he has fought and died for the gods and will continue to fight, but needs to know whether the work matters. The mist still troubles him: even after the rescue, he struggles against the wish to run back toward the daughter he believed he saw. When Elenia asks whether he has tried asking, he answers, “This is me trying.”

Olokun supports the request while saying the discussion will not change his decision to oppose Death. He then turns his attention back to Oya. The questions matter differently to the people in the room; the gathering does not produce a shared judgment on the gods or verify a new history of the world.

The prayers they actually make

Arjahn calls Talan by name, recalls an earlier conversation and asks for honesty in return for the honesty expected of him. He wants to know how the war stands and how the Gate works. He explicitly allows for a later answer. This appeal does not establish that he has renounced another divine relationship.

Nymera looks toward a wall and asks Cala why she was chosen. She says she is trying and asks whether Cala will speak with her. Oya offers a prayer for Namo’o to hear them, remembering the kindness she associates with him. Alyhotep prays too, says his own gods feel distant and offers to keep asking or help the others.

Adelia attempts to reach the Tower’s altar and calls on Nuru. Scribonia later sends his own requests to Cala and Nuru, asking for a meeting with either the gods or their representatives. Elenia says speaking with the gods is a gift she does not want to abuse; she also attempts an intervention before departure. None of those attempts is a confirmed appearance or an answered audience in the surviving sequence.

The distinction matters for what follows. The group has made the request that Scribonia proposed at Skylight Refuge. No formal divine assembly or agreed answers follow before the company leaves.

A way home, money for Oya and an unanswered tap

After his appeal, Arjahn says he cannot transport himself for a week and asks for help returning to Babel-Ashur. Elenia offers to take them, while Scribonia says he has spent his most powerful spells getting everyone together. Arjahn thanks Elenia and tells her that he still cares for her despite the frustration. Their disagreement has not made her cease to matter to him.

Olokun checks Oya’s uncovered hands, feet and movements. The scene shows no visible sign of what he fears, while the argument has left her shaking. He puts an arm around her, then later tells her to stay and help protect Gael because Babel remains dangerous. He trusts her with work at home; the exchange does not grant her an unrecorded office.

They still tease each other. Olokun trips her during a hug, and she tells Arjahn to annoy him with a supposed fear of blobfish. Arjahn does not know what the fish is, so she makes him a quick drawing. Nymera gives Oya money she says is not useful to her in Babel, embraces her and promises to keep trying to make the world better for her.

The company steps through a Gate. Alyhotep gathers his helpers and leaves Lois a note before following. The departures are recorded; arrival at the destination is not shown here. Fenwick’s separate return to the Tower and withdrawal to rest keep the refuge in use beyond the gathering.

In the later narrator follow-up, after the group has dispersed, Arjahn feels a gentle but firm tap on his shoulder. Adelia hears wind, waves and gulls after her appeal, followed by requests for perception and religion checks. No one behind the tap is identified, and no completed check result or divine speech follows. The story pauses with those responses still unresolved.
